structured.approach: I read the two contracted inputs (feat.tasks, org.engineering_stack) and the DE-01 procedure in the data-engineering-steps skill. From feat.tasks I found that the Data Engineering tasks (TSK-01, TSK-02) touch only ap_pipeline. I took availability, branch and write access from the spine's repo-access tool view. Shell commands are blocked in DE-01, so I confirmed the branch state by reading the ap_pipeline .git HEAD and branch refs instead of running git. I confirmed Databricks is not used from org.engineering_stack and from a code search across ap_pipeline for Databricks, Spark, JDBC and database terms, which found nothing. For conventions and notes for later steps I read the repository memory (ap_pipeline/CLAUDE.md), ci.py, src/ap_pipeline/__init__.py and src/ap_pipeline/schedule.json. I did not use any connectors because the inputs and repository files held every fact I needed. The remote URL and committer details in the git log are left out of the output.

claims.text: The Data Engineering lane's tasks TSK-01 (STORY-01) and TSK-02 (STORY-02) both target the ap_pipeline repository.
Repository ap_pipeline is available locally; branch feature/story was created from dev at 3fcbe1b; the agent identity has write access and git status is clean.
HEAD points to refs/heads/feature/story, and main, dev and feature/story all point to commit 3fcbe1bad11e1fb6b44523c7ca795d0c1ca7b1d8.
No repository uses Databricks or a database, so Databricks access is not a prerequisite for this feature.
No repository needs to be created; TSK-02 adds the new module src/ap_pipeline/delays.py and tests/test_delays.py inside the existing ap_pipeline repository.
ap_pipeline uses Python 3.9 and its CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py with coverage >= 90% and static checks standing in for SonarQube.
Code lives in src/ap_pipeline/ and tests in tests/; existing public signatures are kept and new behaviour goes into new functions.
The current ap_pipeline version is 0.4.0, kept in src/ap_pipeline/__init__.py, and TSK-01 owns its version step.
schedule.json sets a daily run at 02:00 Asia/Kolkata, and TSK-01 lists schedule.json under must-not-change.
Commit messages start with the story ID; branches are main (released), dev (integration) and feature/<story>.
ci.py imports the third-party coverage package to measure coverage.

open_questions: RAQ-1 (non-blocking): Is the 'coverage' package that ci.py imports installed for /usr/bin/python3? It was not checked because DE-01 allows no shell commands. Interim answer: assume yes; the first CI run confirms it.
structured.summary: The DE-01 prerequisites are met. ap_pipeline, the only repository for the Data Engineering tasks TSK-01 and TSK-02, is available locally on feature/story (created from dev at 3fcbe1b) with write access and a clean working tree. No repository needs to be created. Databricks does not apply because no repository uses Databricks or a database. task.repo_access.md has been rewritten in full with the availability results, the lane's branch and commit conventions, notes for later steps, and one non-blocking open question about the coverage package that CI needs.
